Sustenance

SUS-tuh-nuns · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Sustenance is food and drink that keeps a person or animal alive and healthy.

The monks' garden provided enough sustenance for the entire monastery through the long winter months.

Worked Example

Astronauts aboard the space station carefully rationed each pouch of dehydrated food, aware that their entire six-month sustenance had to be calculated to the gram before launch.

Sustenance refers to whatever nourishment keeps a living thing alive, from a full meal to the barest rations.

Antonyms

deprivation

deprivation: the lack of something considered necessary

How Strong Is It? — snack → sustenance → feast

snack vs. sustenance

snack vs. sustenance: A snack is a small amount of food eaten between meals, far less than full sustenance.

feast vs. sustenance

feast vs. sustenance: A feast is an abundant, elaborate meal, far more than the sustenance needed simply to survive.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sus-

prefix — sus-: up from below (Latin sub-)

root — ten-

root — ten-: to hold (Latin tenere, 'to hold')

suffix — -ance

suffix — -ance: state or quality of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin sub- ('up from below') plus tenere ('to hold') plus the noun suffix -ance: 'that which holds you up.' Sustenance is the food and drink that keeps a body upright and alive.

Use the root in a new word: maintain

Use the root in a new word: maintain: Regular oil changes help maintain the engine's performance for years.

Root Check

Word Choice

Sustenance can describe anything from a full meal to the barest rations -- the word focuses on the fact that it keeps a living thing alive, not on how much or how tasty it is.
